summary.title: Build a ride hailing app with React Native
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a driver and passenger ride-hailing flow in React Native using Pusher client events, a Node.js auth server, and Google Maps.
keywords: how to build an uber clone
takeaways: How the ride flow works: passenger books, driver accepts, driver location is streamed, and near-pickup and near-destination alerts are sent.
How to set up a Node.js/Express Pusher auth server so private channels and client events can be used.
How to subscribe to private channels and bind client events like client-driver-request in React Native with pusher-js.
How to use watchPosition and a haversine distance helper to trigger proximity messages (50m and 20m thresholds).
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through building a ride-hailing clone with React Native for Android and Pusher for realtime messaging between a driver app and a passenger app. It starts with a Node.js/Express auth server for Pusher private channels, deployed via now.sh, then sets up a React Native project with react-native-maps and react-native-geocoding, including Google Maps API key configuration and Genymotion setup. The core code covers the driver app: listening for ride requests on a private available-drivers channel, handshaking on a per-passenger ride channel, streaming location via watchPosition, and computing distances to send near-pickup and near-destination messages. The page is cut off before the passenger app and the UI details are complete.
